land.text: all of Egypt: 'Nectanebo I had gained control of all of Egypt by November of 380 BC'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria has no row for the Twenty-ninth Dynasty (398-380 BC per the Second Achaemenid conquest page) or the Twenty-eighth (404-398); a dossier is needed. Cliopatria's Thirtieth row starts in -383, three years early.

land.text: Egypt, lost to Artaxerxes III's second invasion in 343 BC ('Succeeded by: Thirty-first Dynasty of Egypt', the Persian kings as pharaohs); the Libyan coast in the shape is not mentioned on the pages

successors.note: Cliopatria's Achaemenid shape of -350..-338 holds only Sinai of Egypt and its shape from -337 holds Egypt (2,108 cells) and Cyrenaica, so the Nile land of 342-338 needs the achaemenid-empire dossier (me-05) to add the Second Egyptian Satrapy from 343; Cliopatria keeps this row to -338.

capitals.name: Sebennytos (Samannud)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Sebennytos'; the page says the dynasty 'moved the capital of Egypt from Mendes to Sebennytos' without a date. Coordinates are the modern town of Samannud (the gazetteer lacks the name).

rulers.name: Nectanebo I
rulers.note: The page's table gives 380-362; its text says 'until his death in 363 BC, father and son reigned together' (co-regency with Teos).

rulers.name: Teos
rulers.note: Deposed 'due to the machinations of his own brother Tjahapimu'.

rulers.name: Nectanebo II
rulers.note: Teos' nephew; fled south to Nubia in 343.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, years only: it holds -380..-367; the three years -383..-381 belong to the Twenty-ninth Dynasty ('founded after the overthrow of Nepherites II in 380 BC')

keyframe_review.note: 687,196 km2. Egypt is 84% of the shape (1,926 of about 2,285 grid cells) and the page says Nectanebo I held 'all of Egypt' from 380; the other 16% reaches the Libyan coast to 18.7E (Cyrenaica and the Gulf of Sidra), which neither page opened mentions: that part is unverified (page budget) and Cliopatria draws the same western edge for the Achaemenid Egypt of -500. Infobox gives no area.

687,438 km2, 243 km2 more than the previous shape and the same footprint. No page event moves the border in 366: Teos' invasion of 'the Persian territories of modern Syria and Israel' (362-360) is not said to have held ground. The Libyan part is unverified as above.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, years only: it holds -350..-343; the dynasty 'was disestablished upon the invasion of Egypt by the Achaemenid king Artaxerxes III in 343 BC', not 338

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the row to -338. The Second Achaemenid conquest page dates the conquest to '340 or 339 BC', the Thirtieth Dynasty page (infobox and text) to 343; the dynasty page is followed. The failed invasion of the winter of 351/350 did not change the border.

ledger.note: 380 BC: Nectanebo I ends the Twenty-ninth Dynasty and rules all of Egypt. 'Nectanebo I had gained control of all of Egypt by November of 380 BC' (month 11 is a latest date); 'he deposed and likely killed Nefaarud II to end the Twenty-ninth Dynasty'; the dynasty 'was founded after the overthrow of Nepherites II in 380 BC'.

region.text: the Nile Delta defences and Memphis

ledger.note: 343 BC: Artaxerxes III invades Egypt a second time. 'was once again able to invade Egypt in 343 BC. This second invasion proved successful'; 'Nectanebo was forced to withdraw from his defenses in the Nile Delta to Memphis'. The page names the Delta and Memphis, not a boundary; the Second Achaemenid conquest page dates the conquest 340 or 339 BC.

region.text: the Nile Delta defences and Memphis

ledger.note: 343 BC: the fighting ends with Nectanebo II's flight. 'He thereupon fled south to Nubia, where he is assumed to have found refuge at the court of King Nastasen of Napata.' Nothing on the page says Nubia held the land of the Delta or became a vassal.

343 BC: Egypt falls to Persia. 'disestablished upon the invasion of Egypt by the Achaemenid king Artaxerxes III in 343 BC'; infobox 'Flight of Nectanebo II: 343 BC'; the Second Achaemenid conquest page gives 340 or 339 BC.

region.text: the part of the Cliopatria shape outside Egypt, along the Libyan coast

ledger.note: The Libyan coast in Cliopatria's shape goes with the dynasty's end; neither page opened mentions Cyrene, Libya or Sinai, so the holder and the year are bridging (Cliopatria's Achaemenid shape of -337 holds Cyrenaica).

region.text: the whole shape: Egypt and the Libyan coast

ledger.note: 343 BC: the last native dynasty of Egypt ends. 'Succeeded by: Thirty-first Dynasty of Egypt' (the Persian kings as pharaohs); Cliopatria keeps the row to -338.

wars.name: Teos' invasion of Persian Syria and Israel
wars.outcome: The page gives no result beyond Teos losing his throne 'due to the machinations of his own brother Tjahapimu'.
wars.note: 'After his father's death, Teos invaded the Persian territories of modern Syria and Israel.' The page gives no year for the campaign (his reign is 362-360) and does not say Egypt held any ground, so no zone and no contest event are drawn.

wars.name: Artaxerxes III's first invasion of Egypt
wars.outcome: Failed: 'Artaxerxes then attempted an unsuccessful invasion of Egypt in the winter of 351/350 BC'.
wars.note: The Second Achaemenid conquest page has the conquest 'after a failed attempt in 351'. No place or battle is named.

wars.name: Second Achaemenid conquest of Egypt

zones.text: the Nile Delta defences and Memphis

wars.outcome: Persian victory: Nectanebo II withdrew from the Delta to Memphis and fled south to Nubia; the Thirtieth Dynasty ended.
wars.note: The Second Achaemenid conquest page has no 343 and places the conquest 'in 340 or 339 BC' (Pelusium's defenders surrendered and Bubastis capitulated, undated); the dynasty page is followed for 343. The Thirtieth Dynasty page names neither Pelusium nor Bubastis.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the Delta, Sinai, Nubian and Libyan edges are approximate, and the Libyan coast in the Cliopatria shape is unverified.

sources.title: Thirtieth Dynasty of Egypt
sources.note: Identity, 380 and 343, capital Sebennytos, rulers table, Teos' campaign, the 351/350 and 343 Persian invasions, Nectanebo II's flight to Nubia. Gives no area and says nothing on Cyrene, Libya, Sinai or the Levant as holdings.

sources.title: Second Achaemenid conquest of Egypt
sources.note: Thin: 351 failed attempt, conquest placed in 340 or 339 BC (disagrees with 343), 28th and 29th dynasty dates. Does not mention Sidon, Nubia, the Second Satrapy or Cyrene.

notes: Cliopatria rows: the -383..-338 row starts three years before the dynasty (380) and ends five years after it (343); both handled as adjusts with the shape unchanged. The Twenty-ninth Dynasty (398-380) and Twenty-eighth (404-398) have no Cliopatria row and no dossier from this group: the 29th is this state's direct predecessor (counterparts_needing_dossiers). Disagreement between pages: the Thirtieth Dynasty page gives 343 BC (infobox and text) for the Persian conquest, the Second Achaemenid conquest page gives 340 or 339 BC; 343 is followed, the end-year events carry confidence 2. The Thirtieth Dynasty page also gives Nectanebo I's death as 363 in the text and 362 in the rulers table. Libya: 16% of the Cliopatria shape (about 359 grid cells, west of Egypt to 18.7E, covering Cyrenaica) is not supported by either page opened, which are silent on Cyrene and Libya; it may be copied from Cliopatria's Achaemenid 'Egypt and Cyrenaica' footprint of -500. A gap-filler with a page on Cyrene in the 4th century BCE should decide whether to remove it. Egypt 342-338: Cliopatria's Achaemenid shape of -350..-338 holds only Sinai of Egypt, so these years need the achaemenid-empire dossier (me-05) to add the Nile land as the Second Egyptian Satrapy from 343. Page budget (1-2 pages) spent on the dynasty article and the Second Achaemenid conquest page. Not on the pages and so not in the ledger: Sidon's revolt, Pelusium and Bubastis, the Nubian frontier, the Levant, Sinai, Cyrene, the date of the capital move from Mendes. Infobox area: none, so the shape's area (687,438 km2) could not be compared. Gazetteer: 'Sebennytos' (Samannud) is not a place name there; capital coordinates were entered by hand.
